providers.title: Irreducibility from the residual representation
providers.scope: An l-adic representation whose residual representation is absolutely irreducible is absolutely irreducible, hence semisimple and determined by its Frobenius characteristic polynomials.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Modularity over imaginary quadratic fields
providers.scope: Every elliptic curve E over an imaginary quadratic field K has an isobaric automorphic representation of GL_2 over K, weight zero and trivial central character, realizing H^1(E) at every prime with matching local parameters, and L(E/K, s) = L(pi_E, s - 1/2). Proved in the eighth lesson, using the named results N1 to N10.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Kummer function
providers.scope: On the twist B_t there is a unique function f_t with divisor (S) - (-S) - n(R) + n(-R) and f_t(O) = 1, where R = (t, 1) and S = [n]R; it satisfies f_t o [-1] = 1/f_t.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Cyclic covers of genus m
providers.scope: For m dividing n, the cover Y^m = f_t is geometrically irreducible of degree m, totally ramified over S and -S and unramified elsewhere, and has genus m.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Fixed points of the involution
providers.scope: The involution w(Z, Y) = (-Z, 1/Y) has exactly four fixed points, one above each 2-torsion point, so C_m/w has genus (m - 1)/2; for m = 3 it is a curve of genus one.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A model of compact type
providers.scope: At the origin of the parameter curve, one blow-up gives a regular semistable model whose special fibre is a rational curve with m copies of E attached, permuted cyclically by the rotations.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Torsion near the origin
providers.scope: For every N, the N-torsion of the Jacobians of the covers near the origin forms a finite etale group scheme with fibre E^m[N] at the origin, compatibly with the rotations. Uses Raynaud's theorem (named result N6).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The node equation
providers.scope: When [n]R tends to a nonzero 2-torsion point, the cover acquires m nodes, each with local equation XU = -2nt in the additive parameter t.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A free module over the group ring
providers.scope: The first homology and cohomology of C_m are free of rank two over the integral group ring of mu_m, for every fibre; hence the l-adic cohomology is free over Z_l[mu_m] for every prime l, including l dividing m.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Picard-Lefschetz transvections
providers.scope: In one integral basis the monodromy contains two transvections whose off-diagonal entries in the group ring are +-(2 - u - 1/u), u a generator of the deck group.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Rank-two systems
providers.scope: Each character piece V_theta of H^1(C_n) is two-dimensional with determinant the inverse cyclotomic character, potentially semistable with Hodge-Tate weights 0 and 1, and part of a compatible system.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The congruence chain
providers.scope: With chi = eta psi of orders 3p, 3, p: V_eta = V_chi mod p, V_chi = V_psi mod 3, V_psi = V_1 mod p, with V_eta = H^1(A_t) and V_1 = H^1(B_t).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Local constancy of the semistable type
providers.scope: In a p-adic family of abelian varieties whose torsion forms finite etale families, the toric rank and the Newton polygon of nearby members equal those of the special member over a fixed finite extension.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Full monodromy in the toric case
providers.scope: An abelian variety of dimension g with potentially totally toric reduction has monodromy of rank g at every coefficient prime, including the residue characteristic.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The trivial character
providers.scope: If G_K acts on E[p] through a group containing SL_2(F_p), then H^1(B_t) mod p is absolutely irreducible and decomposed generic over F = K(mu_3p), for every parameter t.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Specialization with local conditions
providers.scope: A connected Galois cover of an open subset of affine space over Q has a rational point in prescribed p-adic open sets with surjective specialization. Uses the counting form of Hilbert's irreducibility theorem (named result N5).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: One specialization
providers.scope: There is a parameter t in K, inside prescribed local open sets, for which all residual representations of the chain are absolutely irreducible and decomposed generic and A_t has no complex multiplication.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The three lifts
providers.scope: H^1(B_t) over F is modular: automorphy passes from H^1(A_t) along the congruences at p, 3 and p by the Caraiani-Newton lifting theorem (named result N1).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Cyclic descent
providers.scope: For a cyclic extension of CM fields of prime degree, a representation that is automorphic and absolutely irreducible on the larger field is automorphic over the smaller one. Uses base change and strong multiplicity one (named result N3).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
